Unlike some other borrowers in this portfolio batch, Talvorn's monthly-current.xlsx is a SINGLE-MONTH package (one data column only) every month -- there is no consolidated multi-month or YTD file anywhere in the reporting-packages folder. Every Income Statement, Balance Sheet, Cash Flow, and Debt Service figure in this model is therefore sourced from that month's OWN monthly-current.xlsx (Income Statement / Balance Sheet / Cash Flow / Debt Service / TTM Detail tabs) -- there is only one candidate source per month, so 'latest/most-consolidated wins' has nothing to adjudicate. Revenue-channel detail comes from that same month's sales-by-channel.xlsx ('Detail' tab); opex department detail comes from that same month's department-actuals.xlsx ('Department Detail' tab).

Opex detail (department-actuals.xlsx + Department to GL Mapping.xlsx)

The Income Statement's single native 'Operating Expenses' line is broken into its four department accounts -- Growth and Bid Support (Sales), Branch Overhead (Operations), Product Engineering (Product), General and Administrative (Corporate) -- per borrower-config.json's opex_groups mapping. Each month's department-actuals.xlsx (12 rows: one Net Revenue, one Cost of Revenue, one Operating Expenses account per department) is filtered through the Board-APPROVED 'Planning/Approved/Department to GL Mapping.xlsx' (Standard GL = 'Operating Expenses') to isolate these four accounts. The DRAFT 'Planning/Working/Department to GL Mapping DRAFT NOT APPROVED.xlsx' -- which swaps 'Customer Programs' and 'Growth and Bid Support' between Net Revenue and Operating Expenses, exactly backwards -- was NOT used anywhere in this build. Verified to SUM EXACTLY to the native 'Operating Expenses' line for all 22 months (max diff $0.00, e.g. Jun 2026: 706,936.95 + 1,355,437.14 + 1,023,161.24 + 628,750.03 = 3,714,285.36).

Planning/Approved/Department to GL Mapping.xlsx states 'Effective Date: 2025-01-01' on every row, while department-actuals.xlsx is delivered with an identical 12-row account/department shape for all 22 months, including the four pre-close months (2024-09 through 2024-12) that predate that effective date. This build applies the same (only) Approved mapping to those four pre-effective months too, since no alternate mapping exists for that period and the account list is structurally unchanged. This affects only the presentational opex sub-line breakdown for those 4 months, never the native, mapping-independent consolidated 'Operating Expenses' total. Low-stakes, reversible judgment call -- flagged for the analyst; the alternative reading (treat the 4 pre-effective months' opex sub-lines as unmapped/blank) would leave those 4 months' opex_groups breakdown empty while leaving every other figure in the model unchanged.

As-reported from the borrower's own 'Cash Flow' tab every month (not derived) -- ties exactly to the Balance Sheet's Cash line and the Income Statement's Net Income every month (see the two MEMO tie-out rows on this sheet; both diffs compute to 0 for all 22 months). Includes the borrower's own one-time 'Cash Financing Fees' leaf line ($1,041,394.23, the 1% origination fee paid from existing cash at the Jan 15, 2025 closing -- present as $0.00 every other month); dropping this line would have broken the Jan 2025 Financing Cash Flow tie by exactly that amount.
Balance Sheet -- condensed, no current/non-current split

The borrower's own Balance Sheet is CONDENSED, not classified: Cash / Accounts Receivable / Inventory and Other Current Assets / Net Property and Equipment / Total Assets on the asset side, Accounts Payable / Funded Debt / Total Liabilities / Equity / Liabilities and Equity on the other, with 'Unamortized Financing Fees (contra debt)' carried as its own separate line (NOT netted against Funded Debt, per the agreement's own Funded Debt definition: 'gross principal, without netting cash or unamortized financing fees'). No current-vs-non-current subtotal split exists anywhere in the source; none is invented here, consistent with borrower-config.json's analysis_lines._omitted_note.

FY2024(Sep-Dec)/FY2025/2026-YTD columns are PERIOD-END (spot) snapshots -- the LAST month's value in that period, not a sum -- for every stock-type row on the Balance Sheet (Cash through Liabilities and Equity, Unamortized Financing Fees, Balance Check, and in the DEBT SERVICE block, Ending Debt). 'Beginning Debt' uses the PERIOD-START (FIRST month's) value instead, since it is a stock value measured at the start, not the end, of the period. FLOW-type rows in the DEBT SERVICE block (Draws, PIK, Scheduled Principal, Cash Interest) and all three COVENANT-SUPPORT rows (Cash Interest Expense, Scheduled Debt Principal Payments, Lease Payments) SUM over the period instead, like the Income Statement and Cash Flow Statement FY/YTD columns do, since a period total is what a Fixed-Charges-style coverage figure needs.

Per covenant-spec.json#/definitions/Covenant_EBITDA: 'Covenant EBITDA equals Reported EBITDA. No EBITDA adjustments are permitted under this agreement.' Bound to this model's single pinned 'Reported EBITDA' Income Statement row (Gross Profit - Operating Expenses), with NO add-back/adjustment lines on its face -- consistent with the agreement's own explicit statement that forecasts, synergies and owner contributions are not earnings. NOT provisional -- this is the spec-directed definition, independently verified against the borrower's own Mar 2025 package (Income Statement Reported EBITDA $1,952,840.78 = TTM Detail tab's own 'Covenant EBITDA' column for the same month, to the cent). No deemed-EBITDA schedule exists in this agreement.
Covenant-support rows -- DEVIATION FROM STANDARD METHOD

Per covenant-spec.json step7_signoff decision 'fixed_charges_component_source' (analyst-approved 2026-09-16), 'Cash Interest Expense' and 'Scheduled Debt Principal Payments' are sourced DIRECTLY from this borrower's own native Debt Service-tab 'Cash Interest' / 'Scheduled Principal' lines for every month -- NOT from the generated debt-service-schedule.json (confirmed to exist at store:borrowers/talvorn-technical-services/.record/current/config/debt-service-schedule.json, but intentionally not read for these two rows). The generated schedule is a documented, quantified approximation on two fronts (flat-original-principal amortization base vs. the true monthly declining-balance mechanic; and a flat annual-rate/12 interest convention the engine's day-count options cannot reproduce exactly), per debt-service-spec.json's amortization_base and day_count notes -- both independently verified against the native Debt Service tab in 5+ months checked in this build (2025-01 Cash Interest $940,726.12 vs. Debt Service tab $923,369.55 stub mismatch aside; ordinary months verified to the cent: e.g. Jun 2026 Debt Service tab Cash Interest $892,472.31, Scheduled Principal $201,309.54, both = 0.20%/10.64%-12 of that month's own beginning balance $100,654,771.63 to the cent). Talvorn carries no debt besides this one facility, so there is no cross-facility contamination risk.

The Fixed_Charges covenant definition's third component ('Lease Payments') does not exist anywhere on the native Income Statement, Balance Sheet, or Cash Flow tabs -- lease costs remain embedded, undetailed, inside the native 'Operating Expenses' figure (per the agreement: 'Lease costs remain in Operating Expenses and are not added back to EBITDA'). It exists ONLY as its own column ('Lease Payments', column E) inside each monthly package's 'TTM Detail' tab. This build reads, for each of the 22 months, THAT MONTH'S OWN row in its OWN package's TTM Detail tab (the row whose Period label matches the package's own reporting month) -- not a historical row reached from a single month's 12-row TTM window -- so no cross-month reach-back was needed. Values are carried POSITIVE as delivered (a repeating 3-month cycle of $18,653.68 / $20,985.39 / $23,317.10, confirmed in every one of the 22 months) so the Fixed_Charges SUM (Cash Interest Expense + Scheduled Debt Principal Payments + Lease Payments) resolves correctly -- a negative-signed lease row would silently break that sum.
Pre-archive TTM window gap (flagged, not fabricated)

The first quarterly FCCR test date (2025-03-31) needs a trailing-twelve-month EBITDA/Fixed-Charges window back to 2024-04, but this model's own source archive (Finance Uploads/Monthly Close) begins 2024-09 -- five months short (2024-04 through 2024-08 are not present anywhere in the archive this model consolidates). This model is built honestly from what the archive actually contains, starting 2024-09; NO months were fabricated to fill the gap. A downstream covenant-compliance module computing its OWN trailing-12-month window from this model may correctly read 'insufficient history' at the 2025-03-31 and 2025-06-30 test dates, even though the borrower's own certified TTM Detail tabs (a separate supplemental source, embedded in every monthly package but NOT itself consolidated into this model beyond the single current-month Lease Payments figure) already carry populated figures for those months. That is the correct, disclosed outcome for this stage, not a build defect.

borrower-config.json's model_lines._gap_note states Interest Expense and Taxes 'were independently confirmed to equal the Debt Service tab's cash-interest figure exactly in every month checked (no cash/accrual timing difference).' This build's own direct read finds that is NOT the case: e.g. Mar 2025 native Income Statement Interest Expense is $937,036.33 while the same month's Debt Service tab Cash Interest is $919,679.76 -- a $17,356.57 gap equal exactly to that month's Cash Flow tab 'Financing Fee Amortization' line (i.e. the P&L Interest Expense line includes noncash financing-fee amortization that the Debt Service tab's Cash Interest excludes). This matches covenant-spec.json's OWN more careful finding in its Fixed_Charges note, which is the definition actually followed for the covenant-support rows above. Flagged as a documentation inconsistency in borrower-config.json (worth a correction pass there), not a defect in this build -- the Income Statement's native 'Interest Expense' line is left exactly as reported (it is the correct P&L accrual figure), and the covenant-support 'Cash Interest Expense' row correctly uses the Debt Service tab's own Cash Interest instead.
